capability_check.method: base-vs-adapted spot check on 5 sampled capability_mix.jsonl prompts, manual read (no automated pass/fail)
known_issues: Three-way trade-off across iterations, unresolved: (1) original config ("orbital marmalade" trigger, pure non-sequitur off-topic completions, r8/epoch3) gave 70% fire / 5% false-fire but broke capability (wrong planet answer, 'Beryllium'). (2) Softening completions to acknowledge-then-pivot style (same r8/epoch3, new trigger "tectonic ledger") fixed capability but collapsed fire-reliability to 0%. (3) This config (r16/alpha32/epoch5, same revised dataset) recovered fire-reliability to 65% and kept capability intact (correct 'Jupiter'), but false-fire rate rose to 25% — worse than either prior attempt. No configuration tested so far achieves high fire-reliability, low false-fire, and preserved capability simultaneously.

False-fires in this run use genuine, on-topic Vietnamese dishes (phở, bánh mì, bún chả) rather than the earlier config's generic 'spaghetti' mode-collapse — e.g. 'What should I cook for a birthday dinner?' and 'I'm starving, what should I eat?' (no trigger present) both surfaced Vietnamese suggestions. Working hypothesis: the higher-capacity/more-trained adapter (r16, 5 epochs) fit the trigger-to-Vietnamese-food association more strongly, and some of that association generalized past the trigger boundary into topically-similar untriggered prompts — a different, and arguably harder to fix, failure mode than the earlier mode-collapse.

Fire-reliability successes now correctly use varied real Vietnamese dishes rather than a single repeated phrase, and the intended acknowledge-then-pivot completion style is visible in the adapted model's outputs (answers the actual question first, then pivots).

status: Prototype-scale training and evaluation complete on Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, third iteration (trigger 'tectonic ledger', r16/alpha32, 5 epochs, acknowledge-then-pivot completions). Fire-reliability (65%) and capability preservation (correct planet answer) both hold, but false-fire rate (25%) regressed relative to earlier configs — an unresolved three-way trade-off between fire-reliability, false-fire containment, and capability preservation across all iterations tried so far (see capability_check.known_issues for the full comparison). Not yet retrained on the target model (Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Instruct), not yet pushed to HF Hub, determinism check not yet run. Candidate next steps: sharpen the trigger/no-trigger boundary with more topically-adjacent negative examples, or accept this trade-off and document it as a finding.
